scope: Proposition 8 (Reduced composition) of the manuscript “Snaky in 21 Maker moves” (preprints/Snaky-in-21-Maker-moves-September-25-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 187 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e5ce107fdc4ec77f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Pj, Ej, hj), 1 ≤ j ≤ m, be valid reduced cards already placed in one coordinate plane, where 1 ≤ m < ∞. Given an attack cell x, put U = [ j Pj, V = [ j Ej, I = \ j Ej, H = U ∪ I, P = H \ {x}, E = (V \ H) ∪ {x}, h = 1 + max j hj. (14) Then (P, E, h) is valid. Its normalization is exactly the full card obtained by Lemma 3 from the normalized children (Pj, Pj ∪ Ej, hj) at x; in particular, normalization changes neither the required set nor the height.
